subject: radiology
title: Left Atrial Enlargement, Double Atrial Shadow and Cardiac MRI

steps.title: Double density inside the heart shadow
steps.tx: **Double atrial shadow** is a second curved density seen through the right heart border, the enlarged left atrium peeking out behind the right atrium. It is the frontal film signature of left atrial enlargement, most often from mitral stenosis. The left atrium enlarges upward and backward first, so this double density joins splaying of the carina and a lifted left main bronchus in the full sign set.

steps.tx: **Double atrial shadow** is a second curved density seen through the right heart border, the enlarged left atrium showing behind the right atrium. It is the frontal signature of left atrial enlargement, most often from mitral stenosis. One border without those bronchial signs is an incomplete reading of the same enlargement.

steps.title: Mitral stenosis drives atrial enlargement
steps.tx: **Mitral stenosis** narrows the valve until left atrial pressure climbs and the chamber dilates, exactly the progression the illustration traces from valve narrowing to pulmonary congestion. Rheumatic disease fuses the commissures into a fish mouth valve, most patients are women, and symptoms often declare in pregnancy when cardiac output rises. The film then adds upper lobe venous diversion and Kerley lines as pressures climb further.

steps.title: Straightened left heart border
steps.tx: **Mitralised heart** straightens the left border when the enlarged left atrial appendage fills the normal concavity below the pulmonary segment. Four bumps then stack down the left border: aortic knuckle, pulmonary artery, atrial appendage and left ventricle. Loss of the appendage concavity is an early film clue that precedes frank cardiomegaly, which is why examiners crop the left border into spot questions so often.

Four bumps then stack down the border: aortic knuckle, pulmonary artery, appendage and ventricle. Loss of that concavity is an early clue preceding frank enlargement of the whole heart.

steps.title: Carinal angle and bronchial lift
steps.tx: **Carinal splaying** widens the angle between the main bronchi beyond about 90 degrees as the enlarging left atrium pushes up from below. The left main bronchus also turns horizontal, sometimes called the walking man appearance on the lateral film. On barium swallow the same atrium indents the oesophagus from the front, a classic indirect sign from the era before echocardiography measured the chamber directly.

steps.title: Coronary calcium scoring
steps.tx: **Coronary calcium score** quantifies calcified plaque on a non contrast cardiac CT using the Agatston method, multiplying plaque area by a density factor. Zero excludes calcified plaque and carries a strong negative prediction in symptomatic low risk patients, while scores above 400 mark heavy burden needing aggressive prevention. The score sees only calcified plaque, so a symptomatic patient with zero calcium still needs functional or angiographic assessment.

Zero carries strong negative prediction in low risk patients, while above four hundred marks heavy burden. It sees only calcified plaque, so symptomatic patients still need further assessment.

steps.title: CT coronary angiography
steps.tx: **CT coronary angiography** images the coronary lumen with iodinated contrast timed to a bolus, electrocardiogram gating and heart rate control near or below 65 beats per minute. Its strength is a very high negative predictive value in low to intermediate risk chest pain, clearing patients for discharge. Heavy calcification blooms and overstates stenosis, and irregular rhythm blurs segments, which remain its two practical limits at the reporting desk.
steps.say: CT coronary angiography images the coronary lumen with contrast, electrocardiogram gating and heart rate control near sixty five beats per minute. Its strength is a very high negative predictive value in low to intermediate risk chest pain. Heavy calcification overstates narrowing, and irregular rhythm blurs segments, its two practical limits.

steps.title: Cardiac MRI tissue character
steps.tx: **Cardiac MRI** separates scar, oedema and infiltration where echocardiography only shows thickness and motion. Late gadolinium enhancement lights up scar ten minutes after contrast: subendocardial in infarction territories, mid wall in dilated cardiomyopathy and patchy basal in myocarditis. T2 weighted images show the oedema of acute injury, so pairing both sequences dates a lesion and names its pattern in one sitting.

Late gadolinium enhancement lights up scar: subendocardial after infarction, mid wall in dilated cardiomyopathy and patchy in myocarditis. T2 images show acute oedema, so pairing both sequences dates a lesion and names its pattern.

steps.title: Double density versus pericardial fat
steps.tx: **Pericardial fat pad** mimics atrial enlargement at the cardiophrenic angles, but it reads less dense than heart muscle and never splays the carina or lifts a bronchus. The double atrial shadow instead matches soft tissue density exactly and curves parallel inside the right border. Checking the carina and left bronchus on the same film settles the mimic without extra radiation, a favourite examiner trap in both directions.
